question: Which among the following is a unit of measurement that describes the rate at which the universe is expanding?
solution:
The Correct answer is **Hubble**** constant** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points:__

__
 
• 'Expanding Universe'

 
 
• Edwin Hubble, an American astronomer, was the first to prove that the universe is expanding.
 
• According to Expanding Universe theory, the universe is presently expanding.
 
• Hubble proved that there is a direct relationship between the speeds of distant galaxies and their distances from Earth.
 
 
 
• This is now known as Hubble’s Law.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information:__****Faraday:**

 
• When an electric current passes up to 1 second due to 96485 C, through an electrolyte then the equivalent weight of the electrolyte deposited is one & this amount of electric current is called 1 Faraday.
 
• Faraday constant (F) = 96485C mol−1
 
• The constant is named after the British physicist Michael Faraday.
 
• It is a universal constant.
 
• It is the amount of electric charge carried by 1 mole of electrons.
 
• Represented by *F* & its measuring unit is Coulombs per mole (C.mol-1 ).
